newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Hotels seeks nod for term loans.
newsitem.headline: Indian Hotels seeks nod for term loans.

text.p: Leading hospitality firm Indian Hotels Company said it will seek shareholder approval to raise upto 231 million rupees through two term loans to part-finance hotel projects in the western state of Rajasthan.
The company's annual shareholders' meeting is scheduled to be held on September 24 in Bombay, its annual report said.

The firm's annual report said it will seek permission for a loan of upto 150 million rupees from the Tourism Finance Corporation of India Ltd and a loan of upto 81 million rupees from the Industrial Finance Corporation of India Ltd.
Indian Hotels will use the funds to part-finance two hotel projects -- at Jaipur and Jaisalmer -- in Rajasthan state.
The firm said it had commissioned a new air catering unit in Bombay during 1996/97 (April-March).
"The unit in Delhi is undergoing renovation. With both domestic and international airlines increasing their flights, we expect continued growth in business," the report said.
The company said it was also constructing an air catering unit in Calcutta.

Indian Hotels said it had acquired an 11-acre site in Calcutta where it planned to build a hotel of "international standards." It said two new luxury hotels in Bombay and one in Madras were also underway.
